The ~₹30,000 crore QRSAM order, which accounts for over half of BEL's FY27 order inflow guidance of ₹55,000 crore, has faced procedural delays from the Ministry of Defence and is now expected by March 2027.
Base order inflows fell 31% YoY in Q2 FY27 as MoD ordering has yet to ramp up meaningfully, with Q2 inflows of only ~₹3,800 crore.

EBITDA margin contracted ~140-156 bps YoY to ~28% in Q2 FY27, with H1 FY27 operating margin at 26.6% versus 28% full-year guidance, driven by raw material costs rising to 54% of sales from 48% a year ago.
Cost of materials jumped 55% YoY to ₹3,041 crore in Q1 FY27, significantly outpacing the 25% revenue growth and compressing EBITDA margin to 25.1% from 28.1%.
BEL declined ~14% over six months and ~4% YTD as of mid-October, while the Nifty India Defence index rose 10.99% and 19.40% over the same periods respectively.
Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15-20% and order inflow target above ₹55,000 crore, with R&D spending projected above ₹2,200 crore.
Board approved increasing authorised share capital from ₹750 crore to ₹1,000 crore, approved by 99.75% shareholder vote in August; no linked bonus, rights issue, or fundraise has been announced.
P75I submarine-related orders, part of BEL's longer-term pipeline, have been potentially deferred to FY28, while BEL has submitted a bid for the AMCA project in consortium with L&T.
P75I submarine orders deferred to FY28
Q2 FY27 revenue grew 27% YoY to ₹7,291 crore (vs estimate of ₹6,528 crore), net profit rose 19.8% YoY to ₹1,541 crore (vs consensus ₹1,345 crore), beating estimates across revenue, EBITDA, and PAT.
Q2 FY27 beats on all metrics
Order book stood at ₹68,720 crore at end of Q2 FY27, representing 2.3x trailing 12-month sales and providing strong multi-year revenue visibility.
Operating cash flow swung to ₹1,470 crore in H1 FY27 from an outflow of ₹880 crore in H1 FY26, with free cash flow of ₹940 crore versus negative ₹1,330 crore a year ago.
Cash flow sharply improved in H1
BEL shares closed 4.56% higher at ₹397.10 on Nov 4, delivering a 9.17% weekly return and rebounding sharply from the 52-week low of ₹354.55 hit on October 23.

BEL secured orders worth ₹1,011 crore on Oct 21 for AESA radars, sonar systems and jammers, adding to ₹533 crore disclosed on Oct 13, with total recent order inflows reaching ~₹2,452 crore across Aug-Oct.

Near-term catalysts include ~₹20,000 crore Next Generation Corvette electronics opportunity expected by FY27-end, plus Shatrughat, Samaghat, HAMMER orders, and growing traction in drones and counter-drone systems.
BEL carries zero debt with cash and bank balances of ₹1,888 crore and FY26 operating cash flow of ₹1,541 crore, comfortably covering guided FY27 capex of ₹1,200 crore+.

BEL delivered a strong Q2 FY27 that beat estimates on revenue, EBITDA, and PAT, triggering a sharp rebound from its October lows. Key risks are margin compression from rising material costs (H1 margin at 26.6% vs 28% guidance) and the delay of the pivotal ~₹30,000 crore QRSAM order. The trend is improving near-term on strong Q2 results, but sustained re-rating depends on QRSAM materializing by March 2027 and margins recovering toward full-year guidance.
The stock trades at a PE of 43.44x on a TTM basis, which is elevated and leaves limited room for earnings disappointment.
Price-to-book of 10.58x is steep for an industrials company, implying the market has priced in significant future growth.
TTM profit growth has decelerated to 12% compared to the three-year CAGR of 27%, signalling a potential slowdown in earnings momentum.
Debtor days stand at 170 days, indicating significant delays in receivable collection, which is typical of government-dependent businesses but ties up working capital.
Working capital days have expanded sharply from 79.4 to 135 days, putting pressure on free cash flow generation despite strong reported profits.
The stock is down 13% over the past one year and trades roughly 20% below its 52-week high of ₹473.45, indicating ongoing price weakness.
A dividend yield of only 0.66% offers minimal income cushion for investors in a period of elevated interest rates.
Heavy dependence on government defence orders exposes the company to risks from budgetary delays, order deferrals, and policy shifts in defence spending.
The company is virtually debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0, giving it significant financial flexibility and resilience through business cycles.
Return on equity stands at 25.09% (TTM) with a three-year average of 28% and a ten-year average of 24%, reflecting consistently high capital efficiency.
Return on capital employed of 31.88% indicates the company generates strong returns well above typical cost-of-capital benchmarks.
Compounded profit growth of 24% over five years and 27% over three years demonstrates a sustained earnings acceleration trajectory.
Revenue growth of 20% on a TTM basis outpaces the five-year compounded sales growth of 14%, suggesting improving top-line momentum.
The stock has delivered a 10-year CAGR of 25% and a five-year CAGR of 41%, reflecting long-term wealth creation for shareholders.
A healthy dividend payout ratio of 34.5% shows the company balances growth reinvestment with consistent shareholder returns, yielding 0.66% at the current price.
As a leading defence electronics manufacturer, BEL benefits from India's rising indigenous defence procurement budgets and policy push for self-reliance in defence equipment.
